BudgetWise is an ASP.NET Core Web API and React TypeScript personal-finance training app: .NET 8, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS.

**Conventions:** C#: PascalCase types/methods/properties, camelCase locals/parameters; descriptive names; focused methods, composition over inheritance, C# 12 where appropriate, `var` when type is obvious, `using` inside namespaces. Frontend: TypeScript with strict checking; React hooks and functional components; focused, reusable components; Tailwind utilities, no inline styles; semantic HTML and accessibility (ARIA, keyboard navigation). Use constructor dependency injection and appropriate service lifetimes. Use minimal APIs or controllers consistently; REST nouns/HTTP methods; controller actions return `IActionResult` or typed results. Validate with Data Annotations; use built-in middleware, separate request/response DTOs (immutable DTOs as `record`s), explicit domain/DTO mapping. Add XML documentation to all public classes/methods, with `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>` where applicable; comments explain why. Mark incomplete features `// TODO:` with a clear description.

**Testing:** xUnit; React Testing Library; AAA; descriptive names `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`; `WebApplicationFactory<T>` for integration tests; mock external dependencies; cover success, failures, edge/boundary cases, accessibility, and user interactions (not implementation). Use Testing Library `screen` queries; mock APIs with MSW (Mock Service Worker) or similar.

**API/data:** GET/read, POST/create, PUT/update, DELETE/delete; appropriate status codes (200 OK, 201 Created, 404 Not Found, 400 Bad Request, etc.); plural resource paths (e.g. `/api/expenses`), IDs as path variables, filters/search as query parameters. Use DTOs for complex payloads, Data Annotations or FluentValidation, meaningful errors, camelCase JSON, proper Content-Type headers. Use in-memory collections for development/testing; populate realistic representative data via `MockData` in `Data/MockData.cs`; thread-safe collections where needed. Models: property-based initialization, navigation properties, appropriate nullable references (`?`), `required` for mandatory C# 11+ properties.

Some features are intentionally marked with `// TODO` for workshop exercises. When implementing TODO items, follow existing code patterns. Write tests for new features; update documentation. Prioritize clarity over cleverness; keep code beginner-friendly, explain .NET Core and React concepts, demonstrate best practices. For changes: inspect similar code; follow ASP.NET conventions and existing frontend patterns; handle errors and validate; add tests, XML docs for public APIs and JSDoc for TypeScript; validate backend inputs with Data Annotations and forms client-side; return typed results/status codes; ensure frontend/backend coherence.

❌ Do not use service locator pattern (always use dependency injection)
❌ Do not return null from API endpoints (use `NotFound()` or throw exceptions)
❌ Do not put business logic in controllers (use services)
❌ Do not ignore exceptions or use empty catch blocks
❌ Do not use `any` type in TypeScript (use proper types or `unknown`)
❌ Do not create side effects in React component render functions

**Commands**
```sh
cd budgetwise-app/backend
dotnet restore              # Restore dependencies
dotnet build                # Build the project
dotnet run                  # Start the API server (port 5000)
dotnet test                 # Run tests
dotnet watch run            # Run with hot reload
cd budgetwise-app/frontend
npm install                 # Install dependencies
npm run dev                 # Start dev server with Vite (port 5173)
npm run build               # Production build
npm run preview             # Preview production build
npm run lint                # Run ESLint
npm run test                # Run tests
```

**Project files:** `budgetwise-app/backend/Program.cs` (entry/middleware); `budgetwise-app/backend/Controllers/
